prompt: A quilt block is built from equilateral triangles — every side of each triangle is the same length. What is the measure of each angle in one of those triangles?
hint: A triangle with three equal sides also has three equal angles. Think about the total those angles must share.

hints.text: A triangle with three equal sides also has three equal angles. Think about the total those angles must share.
The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$, and here all three are the same size, so divide $180$ by $3$.
$180 \div 3 = 60$, so each angle is $60^\circ$, which is choice A.

explanation: An equilateral triangle has three congruent sides, and equal sides lie opposite equal angles, so all three angles are congruent.
The Triangle Sum Theorem says those three equal angles must add to $180^\circ$.
Sharing the total equally gives $180 \div 3 = 60^\circ$ for each angle, which is choice A.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why quilters love them
steps: Six equilateral triangles fit around a single point with no gaps, because $6 \times 60 = 360^\circ$ — a full turn.
That is exactly why a $60^\circ$ corner tiles so cleanly into hexagon quilt blocks.
